sentences.text: In April 1976, the Minister of National Health and Welfare announced a mass vaccination program to protect Canadians against a possible pandemic of influenza, which was to cover approximately ten million citizens and would have to be applied in a very short time period.

Federal health authorities coordinated vaccination programs with provincial and territorial partners, with the federal level well placed to coordinate activities such as the procurement of vaccines and antiviral drugs and the sharing of epidemiologic information on infectious diseases.
A vaccination program was implemented to vaccinate high-risk groups including neonates of hepatitis B mothers, health professionals, firemen, policemen, and mortuary attendants.

Federal authorities assisted provinces with B.C.G. vaccination programs for tuberculosis control, with 3.1 percent of tuberculosis program monies expended in Canada used to provide various B.C.G. vaccination programs.

The Health of Animals Branch considered vaccination programs for brucellosis control in Canada, where vaccination reduced the level of infection to a point where it was possible to proceed with a test-and-slaughter program to eradicate the disease.

answer.text: In April 1976, the Minister of National Health and Welfare announced a mass vaccination program to protect Canadians against a possible pandemic of influenza, which was to cover approximately ten million citizens and would have to be applied in a very short time period. Federal health authorities coordinated vaccination programs with provincial and territorial partners, with the federal level well placed to coordinate activities such as the procurement of vaccines and antiviral drugs and the sharing of epidemiologic information on infectious diseases. A vaccination program was implemented to vaccinate high-risk groups including neonates of hepatitis B mothers, health professionals, firemen, policemen, and mortuary attendants. Federal authorities assisted provinces with B.C.G. vaccination programs for tuberculosis control, with 3.1 percent of tuberculosis program monies expended in Canada used to provide various B.C.G. vaccination programs. The Health of Animals Branch considered vaccination programs for brucellosis control in Canada, where vaccination reduced the level of infection to a point where it was possible to proceed with a test-and-slaughter program to eradicate the disease.
